## AI-Assisted Workflow Triage

A shared inbox can become a manual sorting exercise: identify incomplete or
duplicate requests, decide who owns each item and chase work that has waited
too long. This project makes those steps repeatable and gives an AI reviewer
structured evidence for a first review draft.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="review-principles">
  <article><h3>Repeatable intake checks</h3><p>Five controls expose missing fields, duplicate requests, invalid ages, unknown categories and overdue work.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Routing and follow-ups</h3><p>Eligible requests become a proposed queue for Service Desk, Finance or Operations, with overdue follow-ups clearly flagged.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Evidence-grounded AI</h3><p>The AI drafts observations and next steps from the control evidence. A person reviews the brief and approves any action.</p></article>
</div>
```

## What is automated?

The same JavaScript engine runs in the browser and the command-line runner.
It checks the intake, excludes every row in a duplicate group, builds a
routing plan for eligible requests and identifies items older than the chosen
threshold. The route rules are explicit: access requests go to Service Desk,
billing to Finance and general requests to Operations.

An unresolved intake issue blocks release of the batch. Eligible routes remain
visible as diagnostic proposals. A threshold breach calls for review; it does
not prove urgency. Nothing in this demonstration sends a message, creates an
external task or silently changes the source.

## Where AI adds value

The AI step turns the exception register into a short review brief: what needs
attention, what the evidence establishes and what follow-up to request. It
receives aggregate counts, queue totals, the snapshot and control results.
Request subjects, identifiers and row references are excluded.

The public page runs locally in your browser and does not call an AI provider.
The worked example below is AI-authored text prepared for the default
scenario; it is not a saved API response. The downloadable runner implements
the live AI step separately.

```{=html}
<div class="review-ai">
  <h3>Worked AI review · exception inbox at 24 hours</h3>
  <button id="review-show-ai" type="button" class="btn btn-outline-primary" disabled>Show worked AI draft</button>
  <p id="review-ai-note" class="review-ai-note"></p>
  <div id="review-ai-output"></div>
</div>
```

Every flagged control must appear exactly once in the AI output, with its
observed count unchanged. Unknown controls, missing findings, refusals and
incomplete responses fail the AI step. These checks constrain the structure
and cited counts; a person still needs to assess the narrative and approve
any action. AI cannot change the control results or release the batch.

## Reproduce the project

[Download the source and tests](../../assets/automation/workflow-triage-source.zip){.btn .btn-primary}
[Inspect the control engine](../../assets/automation/review-engine.js){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

Extract the source bundle and run these commands from its root with Node.js
22 or later. The workflow and tests use built-in Node modules, with no
package installation or external service required.

```bash
node --test tests/workflow-triage.test.mjs
node projects/workflow-triage/run.mjs
node projects/workflow-triage/run.mjs --scenario clean --threshold 8
```

For a fresh AI draft, provide an API key through your local environment and
choose a model that supports structured outputs. Keep the key outside the
website, source files and shell history. The explicit `--ai` flag sends the
synthetic aggregate evidence to OpenAI and can incur API charges.

```bash
node projects/workflow-triage/run.mjs --ai --model YOUR_MODEL_ID
```

The runner prints the routing plan, control evidence, its SHA-256 fingerprint
and any AI draft as JSON. It requests `store: false`, imposes a request timeout and leaves any
accepted draft awaiting human review. Without `--ai`, it makes no external
request. The integration follows the official [Responses API structured-output
documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

## Scope and limits

The exception fixture contains 14 incoming rows: 8 are eligible for a draft
routing plan and 6 are excluded. All five controls flag an issue at the default
24-hour threshold. The corrected fixture contains 12 eligible requests, split
four per queue, with no overdue requests at that threshold.

This is a working prototype for workflow automation and a bounded AI handoff.
It does not claim production deployment or measured time savings. It uses
small synthetic batches and supplied categories rather than classifying
unstructured emails. A production extension would need an approved inbox
integration, business-calendar rules, access controls, broader tests and
human approval before creating or sending work.
